subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw core define a first-class admin-scoped CLI/Gateway/Control UI notification contract for shell-triggered UI alerts, or should this be folded into plugin/ClawHub or the broader WebUI notification tracker?
rationale: The requested behavior is absent and feasible, but it crosses a security-sensitive admin broadcast boundary plus CLI, Gateway protocol, and Control UI UX surfaces, so automation should not choose the permanent product/API shape.

options.title: Sponsor a core notification contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the focused core design item for a typed admin-scoped CLI/Gateway/Control UI notification path with explicit security controls.

options.title: Fold into WebUI notification architecture
options.body: Move the shell-triggered use case under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/20237 so one broader toast/notification system owns payload semantics and UI behavior.

options.title: Route to plugin or ClawHub extension design
options.body: Close or defer core implementation until a plugin-facing notification/broadcast extension point is intentionally designed.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core notification contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the focused core design item for a typed admin-scoped CLI/Gateway/Control UI notification path with explicit security controls.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main Gateway/CLI/UI carrier lines all point to the recent carrying commit, and the decision spans core product and security boundaries.
